children: GF Securities believes the major hyperscalers are demonstrating the "AI Red Queen Effect," which is driving overinvestments during the AI buildout boom.

The "AI Red Queen Effect" refers to hyperscalers being more willing to risk overinvestment rather than underinvestment to keep pace with rivals and potentially fall behind or lose a competitive advantage.

"We believe the AI race exhibits a Red Queen Effect, where hyperscalers are more willing to risk overinvestment than underinvestment, as slowing capex could cede AI leadership and weaken their competitive positions," said GF Securities analyst Henry Huang in a Tuesday investor report. "Despite our upward-revised capex forecasts, with U.S. Top-5 CSP capex to grow +85%/+53%/+20% in 2026–2028, and widening credit spreads, with 20y+ hyperscaler spreads rising to ~118bps, we expect their balance sheets to remain healthy into 2028, where net leverage (EBITDA basis) is expected to be at 0.6x with interest coverage at 14x, leaving ample headroom for further investment."
The top five U.S. hyperscalers include Microsoft
, Amazon
, Google
, Oracle
and Meta
. GF has also added SpaceX
to this group.
The phenomenon of ever-higher investments in the AI computing space will likely favor the larger players.

"Despite capital availability, investors are becoming more selective on borrower quality, collateral and financing structure, with new issue concessions on some deals rising from 2–3bps historically to ~20bps," Huang noted. "Recent price declines are concentrated in unsecured debt from lower-quality AI issuers, while secured loans backed by chips or lease payments from high-quality vendors remain resilient. The divide is evident between hyperscalers and Neoclouds, with hyperscaler 20y+ spreads at ~118bps vs. CoreWeave
yields rising to ~15% by mid-Oct; within Neoclouds, with larger players retaining funding access while weaker ones face tighter capital."
Executives ranging from Amazon to Amkor
to Nvidia
to TSMC
continue to highlight the fact that demand still outpaces supply despite the rampant buildout.
The scramble has prompted hyperscalers to secure funds from more sources, including private and foreign markets, according to GF Securities.

"Funding structures are also becoming more diversified," Huang said. "As FCF turns negative, hyperscalers are increasingly combining debt with equity, hybrid securities and changes in capital allocation. Alphabet raised $49.6bn through common equity and mandatory convertible preferreds in June; Meta suspended share buybacks this year (vs. $26.2bn in FY25) and launched a $35bn equity offering alongside a $60bn Class C ATM program to preserve capital for AI investment."

title: Hyperscalers demonstrate 'AI Red Queen Effect' to drive overinvestments: GF
